decisions.reason: As a newly launched resin injection unit with its own page and clear fit to our application-technology portfolio, we would keep it and treat any weak early uptake as a normal market ramp-up issue.

Despite some overlap risk with another two-component resin injection unit, we have already invested and publicly committed to it, so management would be inclined to continue rather than withdraw quickly.

An automatic airless spray gun sits very close to our core spraying business, and after a recent launch we would justify continued support on the basis of strategic relevance and early-stage customer adoption.
A manual airless spray gun is highly central to our established product logic and service network, so escalation of commitment makes a near-term withdrawal unlikely.

The air-assisted airless spray gun extends our core finishing and coating offering, and because we have already put it visibly on the market we would likely persist for longer before reconsidering it.

Although the data logger is somewhat more peripheral than the core mechanical equipment, it supports our innovation narrative and documented coating solutions, so we would still tend to keep it while attributing any disappointment to an early commercialization phase.
